subject: Post-call: FinLytics deployment needs & pricing
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finlytics.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: FinLytics deployment needs & pricing

Thanks for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of needs (from our call):
- Initial product integration for customer-facing ML features (chat + summarization).
- Compliance requirement: data residency for US only, potential need for SOC 2 / HIPAA controls depending on data flows.
- Performance target: sub-150ms p50 for interactive flows; peak ~200 QPS discussed.
- Long-term: likely need for predictable throughput and cost stabilization as usage grows.

Deployment options we discussed:
1) Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, pay-as-you-go (per-token). Good for early testing and light production traffic.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved commits): predictable throughput on dedicated GPUs; lower unit cost at scale; supports isolation and higher throughput.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): for strict compliance/regulatory needs; includes customer-managed networking and KMS.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Marcus: can you size a few capacity scenarios (hosted token estimate vs reserved capacity for 100/200/500 QPS) and attach a simple cost worksheet? (Marcus in CC)
- Aditya: I’ll send a mutual action plan and pricing summary once we have Marcus’ numbers.
- Sarah/Tom: confirm whether PHI/PII will be in inference requests and any procurement timelines.

I’m attaching a short worksheet that we’ll refine with Marcus’ numbers. Happy to jump back on a 30-min call after that.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: RE: Post-call: FinLytics deployment needs & pricing

Thanks Aditya — following up with technical sizing/questions and a first-pass cost model (attached worksheet).

A few clarifying Qs to make the numbers accurate:
- Traffic profile: can you confirm expected avg QPS vs peak QPS and whether traffic is bursty (short spikes) vs sustained?
- Request size: typical input tokens and expected output tokens (avg/peak).
- Latency SLO: you mentioned p50 < 150ms — is p95 a hard SLO or target?
- Data flows: will you send full request bodies (with PII) to hosted endpoints, or do you need private networking for complete isolation?

Preliminary sizing notes (assumptions in worksheet):
- Hosted (per-token): good for up to ~50–100 QPS for predictable economic modeling; cost scales linearly. For 200 QPS at ~150 tokens per request (input+output), hosted per-token costs could be approximately $X/day (worksheet shows example numbers) — these are ballpark and depend on model choice and streaming.
- Dedicated (reserved commit): for sustained 200 QPS we recommend a mid-sized reserved pool. Reserved pricing gives ~40–60% effective savings vs hosted per-token at steady-state depending on commit term and utilization. Worksheet includes 1/3/6/12-month commit scenarios.
- Private/VPC: similar unit economics to Dedicated but with addenda for networking, on-prem ops, and potential one-time setup costs.

Attached: finlytics_deployment_options.xlsx (tabs: assumptions, hosted_estimate, dedicated_commit_examples, private_vpc_notes)

I can put together two concrete scenarios for you:
A) Low-friction path (hosted) to go-live in 2–4 weeks for PoC.
B) Dedicated commit plan to support production 200 QPS with pricing options for 6- and 12-month commits.

If you can reply with avg/peak tokens and confirm data sensitivity, I’ll produce exact numbers.

—Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks — quick answers below:
- Traffic: peak ~200 QPS (expected sustained peak windows during business hours), average ~45–60 QPS overall. We will have short spikes up to 250 QPS during promotions.
- Tokens: avg request ~120 tokens input, ~30 tokens output (so ~150 tokens total avg); some long requests can hit ~600 tokens.
- Data sensitivity: some requests will include PII; we are not sure about PHI yet but it’s possible. Compliance is important; we need SOC 2 documentation and may require a VPC option for production.
- Timeline: procurement aims to finalize vendor by end of Q2; PoC in next 4–6 weeks would be ideal.

Please send the hosted vs dedicated cost examples (monthly) and a suggested commit level for Dedicated to hit our 200 QPS target. Also include rough setup times for Private/VPC if we decide that’s required.

Sarah — thanks for the quick answers, this is super helpful. Attached is an updated worksheet (finlytics_deployment_options.xlsx) and a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.pdf) that lays out milestones and owners. High-level pricing summary based on your numbers: 

1) Hosted API (per-token, example using our mid-sized LLM profile):
- Ballpark: $0.00045 per token (example).
- For 200 QPS at 150 tokens avg => ~2.6M tokens/hour => ~62.4M tokens/day.
- Estimated monthly spend (30d): ~ $842k/month (illustrative; exact depends on model and streaming).

2) Dedicated (reserved commit):
- Recommended commit: capacity sized for sustained 200 QPS with headroom for bursts (~250 QPS) — worksheet shows 2 node-pool configs.
- Effective unit cost: roughly 40–55% lower than hosted per-token at high utilization.
- Example commit pricing: $38k–$55k/month depending on commit term and utilization assumptions (see commit buckets in worksheet).

3) Private / VPC / On-prem:
- Similar per-unit economics to Dedicated plus setup and networking fees; setup timeline 4–8 weeks for VPC onboarding, longer if on-prem hardware is required.

Notes and caveats:
- The hosted monthly number looks large at 200 QPS because we’re projecting high sustained throughput; hosted is excellent for PoC and variable loads but becomes expensive for sustained heavy usage.
- Dedicated commits assume strong utilization — savings are realized when committed capacity is used consistently.
- We can provide a SOC 2 package and run a privacy/data flow review; if PHI is in scope we recommend Private/VPC.

Next suggested steps:
- Marcus: finalize two committed-config quotes (6- and 12-month) with exact node counts and exclusive throughput numbers.
- Aditya: I’ll schedule a 30-min pricing review with your procurement/legal teams and share the HubSpot deal link and external Drive folder.
- Sarah/Tom: confirm a good time for next week for the pricing review — I’ve tentatively held Wed 10–10:30 PT if that works.

Links: HubSpot deal record (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567/DEAL-2026-0092), Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1FinLytics-Deal)
